glossdef.p: You don’t technically need a case; however, it will make things much safer and more organized to have everything tucked away inside a case. Cases also allow you to direct airflow using fans in order to keep your components cool.

The most important consideration when getting a case is the form factor. Your case needs to be at least large enough to fit your motherboard and other components. An ATX form factor case is large enough for an ATX motherboard, but can also mount a smaller micro-ATX motherboard. Larger cases also have more room to work in while installing components.

The second most important consideration is how it looks. This is what you will be looking at every time you use the computer. There are cases with lights, transparent panels, and all kinds of color schemes. Or you can get a basic beige box.

Ventilation is also a concern, but most cases will have enough mounting brackets for fans. If a case does not come with fans, buy enough to have at least one intake fan and one exhaust fan. More fans can provide better cooling, albeit with diminishing returns, but they will also create more noise.
